title: The Architecture of Access — Chanel's Handbag Price Ladder in Context
summary: A source-linked study of visible Chanel entry, family steps and Classic anchors, with three brands as external coordinates.

sections.title: Open
sections.summary: The question and its observation boundary.
paragraphs: How does Chanel present visible entry, family-level steps and the Classic high anchor in local official list-price observations?

sections.title: Context
sections.summary: Four brands on separate local price axes.
paragraphs: Chanel is the focal case. Hermès, Louis Vuitton and Dior provide external coordinates; the panel is non-weighted and coverage differs by brand and market.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.summary: A brand point expanded into family positions.
paragraphs: Classic 11.12 and Small Classic form the Classic group. Mini Classic is an entry observation even though its name contains Classic; Shopping Bag and Bowling Bag are other core observations. Price-upon-request rows stay outside the numeric axis.

sections.title: Evolution
paragraphs: The Chanel France history panel compares fixed lineages without interpolating missing years. The values are product-line observations, mostly from secondary historical tables.

sections.title: Interpretation
paragraphs: If the visible distance survives de-variant sensitivity, verify the full SKU ladder and upgrade path. If it moves with family coverage, map the assortment before making a pricing decision.

sections.title: Afterlife
paragraphs: The candidate remains noindex and unpublished. All figures point to R1 outputs; Hermès Geta's 2023 France conflict remains excluded from the core narrative.

claims.text: In the accepted FR numeric snapshot, the lowest Classic observation is 10000 EUR versus a highest entry/core observation of 6700 EUR; the observed gap is 3300 EUR.
claims.scope: Chanel; FR; current_2026-08-15; Classic=Classic 11.12 + Small Classic; comparison=Mini Classic + Shopping Bag + Bowling Bag.
claims.limitation: Accepted observed rows are not a complete assortment and do not establish purchase substitution.

claims.text: In the accepted US numeric snapshot, the lowest Classic observation is 11000 USD versus a highest entry/core observation of 7400 USD; the observed gap is 3600 USD.
claims.scope: Chanel; US; current_2026-08-15; Classic=Classic 11.12 + Small Classic; comparison=Mini Classic + Shopping Bag + Bowling Bag.
claims.limitation: Accepted observed rows are not a complete assortment and do not establish purchase substitution.

claims.text: Dior US has 13 numeric prices among 20 accepted observations (65.0% numeric coverage); unresolved rows remain excluded from price distributions.
claims.scope: Dior; US; current_2026-08-15; accepted observed product rows.
claims.limitation: This is numeric coverage, not official website assortment coverage.

claims.text: The Chanel France icon/access panel has common observed years 2022, 2023, 2024, 2026; the median absolute distance is 4470 EUR in 2022 and 5350 EUR in 2026.
claims.scope: Chanel; FR; fixed CH-C01/CH-C02 versus CH-C03/CH-C04 lineages; common observed years only.
claims.limitation: Historical values are primarily secondary-source observations and continuity is model-level, not exact historical SKU proof.
